fixturePurpose: Phase 19 test fixture and generator self-check input ONLY
warning: This file contains the scenario answer key. It must never be shown to an investigator as a result and must never be used by the analysis pipeline as an input. The product reports a probable origin region with uncertainty.

expectedOriginRegion.note: The ellipse is the scenario's uncertainty region, not a point estimate.

driftModelUsed.description: forward integration of the demo drift field from the release point to the observation

expectedGapFixtures.label: ais_gap_physically_compatible
expectedGapFixtures.reason: synthetic AIS transmission gap inserted by the scenario design

expectedGapFixtures.label: ais_gap_physically_impossible
expectedGapFixtures.reason: synthetic AIS transmission gap inserted by the scenario design

expectedAnomalyFixtures.timing: slow segment covers the release window inside the origin region

expectedAnomalyFixtures.note: included so that a slow vessel far from the origin is NOT promoted

observedVsRelease.teachingPoint: The observed slick is tens of kilometres downstream of the release point, so proximity to the slick is not proximity to the release location.

vesselSummaries.name: DEMO MERIDIAN STAR
vesselSummaries.roleDescription: Inside the probable-origin uncertainty region during the release window with a compatible trajectory and a marked slowdown nearby. Expected highest compatibility.

expected.notes: Slowdown and loitering also have innocent explanations (see methodology).

vesselSummaries.name: DEMO CORAL VOYAGER
vesselSummaries.roleDescription: Inside the origin region when a 4 h AIS gap starts; the gap crosses the region and its endpoints are reachable at a plausible 10.5 kn. Expected high compatibility.

intentionalGaps.label: ais_gap_physically_compatible
intentionalGaps.reason: synthetic AIS transmission gap inserted by the scenario design

expected.hypothesis: AIS gap that is physically consistent with the origin region
expected.notes: Same anchor geometry as V003: the only difference is whether the gap is traversable.

vesselSummaries.name: DEMO IRON HORIZON
vesselSummaries.roleDescription: Inside the origin region when a 4 h AIS gap starts, but reappears ~260 km away - an implied ~35 kn. The gap is physically impossible and must not raise suspicion.

intentionalGaps.label: ais_gap_physically_impossible
intentionalGaps.reason: synthetic AIS transmission gap inserted by the scenario design

expected.hypothesis: AIS gap that is NOT physically compatible with the origin region
expected.notes: Paired with V002 to prove that gap detection alone cannot drive the ranking: the difference is physical feasibility only.

vesselSummaries.name: DEMO HARBOUR LIGHT
vesselSummaries.roleDescription: Closest vessel to the OBSERVED slick at observation time, but far from the probable ORIGIN during the release window. Distractor for proximity-based reasoning.

expected.hypothesis: nearest to the observed slick but spatially incompatible with the origin
expected.notes: A 2 kn loiter near the slick is a behavioural anomaly that must not outweigh location and time.

vesselSummaries.name: DEMO SILVER TIDE
vesselSummaries.roleDescription: Crosses the probable-origin region hours AFTER the release window closes. Correct place, wrong time: expected low temporal compatibility.

expected.notes: Tests that a model collapsing time would wrongly promote this vessel.

vesselSummaries.name: DEMO FROST PELICAN
vesselSummaries.roleDescription: Strong behavioural anomaly (speed swings and 90 degree course changes) ~200 km from the origin region. Anomaly alone must not produce a high rank.

expected.hypothesis: behavioural anomaly without spatial or temporal compatibility
expected.notes: Also carries the negative-SOG and impossible-speed defect rows.

vesselSummaries.name: DEMO NORTHERN GATE
vesselSummaries.roleDescription: Legitimate steady transit ~90 km from the origin region: no anomaly, no gap. Shows that a normal vessel in the same area and time window is not promoted.

expected.hypothesis: control: normal behaviour, insufficient spatial compatibility

vesselSummaries.name: DEMO SEA LARK
vesselSummaries.roleDescription: Many slow and stationary periods and an irregular track, but ~170 km from the origin region. Legitimate working pattern that must not be flagged as suspicious.

expected.notes: Carries the two malformed-timestamp defect fixtures.

vesselSummaries.name: DEMO SKY BRIDGE
vesselSummaries.roleDescription: Fast, steady, predictable shuttle service well north of the origin region. High speed and the 180 degree turnarounds must not be read as suspicious behaviour.

expected.hypothesis: control: high speed and turnarounds are not suspicious by themselves
expected.notes: Instant 180 degree turnarounds are a documented synthetic simplification.

vesselSummaries.name: DEMO COASTAL WREN
vesselSummaries.roleDescription: Slow coastal transit whose track stays offshore and roughly parallel to the coastline - used to test land/sea plausibility rather than suspicion.

expected.notes: In-extract interval is bounded by the study-area box, not by loss of signal.

vesselSummaries.name: DEMO ANCHOR TUG
vesselSummaries.roleDescription: Local harbour movements with long mooring periods ~115 km from the origin region. Stationary periods must not be weighted as suspicious.

vesselSummaries.name: DEMO FAR CURRENT
vesselSummaries.roleDescription: Distant steady transit that should be filtered out early. Included so the ranking is not distorted by irrelevant traffic.
